findings.description: External call _claimRewards(recipient) -> phUSD.mint(user, pendingPhUSDAmount) (line 442) occurs before state writes: totalStaked += amount (321), user.amount/phUSDDebt/stableDebt (316-318) and _updatePhUSDEmissionRate() -> phUSDPerSecond (324/463/469). phUSDPerSecond, totalStaked and userInfo are read by cross-function views/accrual (_updatePool, pendingPhUSD, pendingStable, getPoolInfo, withdraw, claim, pauseWithdraw), so a reentrant callback during mint sees inconsistent accounting.
findings.rationale: Real CEI violation: the reward sink is an external mint() and accounting state is updated after it. phUSD is a protocol-controlled mintable token (mitigates classic attacker control), and the function carries no nonReentrant modifier (only collectReward does) -> dedup/severity must judge whether phUSD.mint can re-enter. Kept (Law 1: recall over tidiness).

findings.description: External call _claimRewards(msg.sender) -> phUSD.mint (line 442) occurs before state writes: totalStaked -= actualWithdrawAmount (359), user.amount/phUSDDebt/stableDebt (354-356) and _updatePhUSDEmissionRate() -> phUSDPerSecond (365/463/469). Same cross-function reentrancy surface as stake (totalStaked, phUSDPerSecond, userInfo).
findings.rationale: CEI violation on the core unstake path; no nonReentrant modifier. The mint() callback could observe pre-decrement totalStaked/user.amount. Kept for recall; severity hinges on whether protocol-owned phUSD.mint can hand control to the caller.

findings.description: External call _claimRewards(msg.sender) -> phUSD.mint (line 442) occurs before state writes user.phUSDDebt (379) and user.stableDebt (380). userInfo is read across _claimRewards, stake, withdraw, pendingPhUSD, pendingStable, pauseWithdraw, allowing a reentrant claim to double-count pending rewards before debt is rebased.
findings.rationale: Debt (reward checkpoint) is written only after the mint external call; a re-entrant claim before line 379/380 would see stale phUSDDebt/stableDebt. No nonReentrant on claim. Kept for recall.

findings.description: phUSD.mint(user, pendingPhUSDAmount) external call (442) followed by RewardsClaimed event emission (453). This internal function is the shared external-call sink reached by stake/withdraw/claim.
findings.rationale: Lower-severity sibling of SLITHER-001/002/003 marking the exact external-call site (the phUSD.mint). Kept as the canonical sink location so dedup can anchor the reentrancy cluster; event-ordering itself is minor but the call site is load-bearing.

findings.description: Precision loss: potentialReward = (rewardPerSecond * timeElapsed) / PRECISION (403); toDistribute = potentialReward (406); then accStablePerShare += (toDistribute * PRECISION) / totalStaked (410). A division (by PRECISION) feeds a later multiplication (by PRECISION), and rewardPerSecond is itself a scaled (rewardBalance*PRECISION)/depletionDuration quotient.
findings.rationale: Core stable-reward accrual math. Linear-depletion rate is divided then re-scaled; rounding can systematically under/over-distribute over many small updates (rate recomputes every interaction in V1 per CLAUDE.md). Security/economic-relevant precision finding -> kept.

findings.description: View mirror of SLITHER-005: potentialReward = (rewardPerSecond * timeElapsed) / PRECISION (503); toDistribute = potentialReward (506); _accStablePerShare += (toDistribute * PRECISION) / totalStaked (509). Same divide-before-multiply ordering as the on-chain accrual.
findings.rationale: Read-side pending-reward preview must match _updatePool exactly; identical rounding so any drift is consistent, but confirms the same precision pattern is reachable via a view. Kept to corroborate SLITHER-005.

findings.description: Reward accrual gated on block.timestamp: 'block.timestamp <= lastRewardTime' (390) and timeElapsed = block.timestamp - lastRewardTime (400) drives the entire stable + phUSD distribution.
findings.rationale: LOAD-BEARING per suite policy: linear depletion accrues over (block.timestamp - lastRewardTime). Not informational here; kept so severity-classifier can assess timestamp/accrual sensitivity.

findings.description: block.timestamp > lastRewardTime && totalStaked != 0 (501); timeElapsed = block.timestamp - lastRewardTime (502) drives previewed stable accrual and the rewardBalance cap.
findings.rationale: LOAD-BEARING: time-driven stable-reward preview. Kept per suite policy (time is the depletion driver).

findings.description: block.timestamp > lastRewardTime && totalStaked != 0 (483); timeElapsed = block.timestamp - lastRewardTime (484) drives previewed phUSD emission accrual.
findings.rationale: LOAD-BEARING: time-driven phUSD APY emission preview. Kept per suite policy.

findings.description: Slither flags withdraw under block-timestamp because it reaches _updatePool; the 'dangerous comparison' it lists is require(user.amount >= amount) (336), which is NOT a timestamp comparison.
findings.rationale: Kept per explicit suite policy (do NOT drop timestamp detectors), but the flagged comparison is a balance check, not block.timestamp -> likely a tainted/spurious attribution from the _updatePool call edge. dedup/severity should down-rank unless tied to SLITHER-007.

findings.description: Slither flags pauseWithdraw under block-timestamp; the listed 'dangerous comparison' is require(user.amount >= amount) (247), not an actual block.timestamp comparison. pauseWithdraw deliberately skips _updatePool (emergency exit).
findings.rationale: Kept per suite policy, but appears spurious (no timestamp comparison in this function; it is the emergency path that intentionally does not accrue). Flagged as likely FP for downstream triage.

findings.description: Slither flags _claimRewards under block-timestamp; the listed comparisons are pendingPhUSDAmount > 0 (441), pendingRewardAmount > 0 (447) and their OR (452) - none are block.timestamp comparisons.
findings.rationale: Kept per suite policy; comparisons are reward-amount guards, not timestamp -> likely spurious attribution. Retained for recall, marked low confidence.

findings.description: setPauser(address _pauser) updates the security-critical 'pauser' state variable (207) without emitting an event, so off-chain monitors cannot observe pauser-role rotation.
findings.rationale: QA/observability gap on a privileged role that controls pause/unpause (and thus pauseWithdraw availability). Owner-only and owner is trusted, but silent rotation of the pauser is a monitoring blind spot worth noting. Kept as low; the companion zero-check finding was dropped because setPauser(0) is documented-intentional ('can be zero address to disable pausing').
